Of course. Here is an introduction to Horsehead Corporation, incorporating its history, business, and connection to the Monaca, Pennsylvania site.

***

Situated at its sprawling industrial complex at 300 Frankfort Road in Monaca, Pennsylvania, Horsehead Corporation was a pivotal, yet complex, figure in the North American metals industry for decades. Though broadly categorized as a chemical and manufacturing company, its primary focus was on zinc. Horsehead was a leading producer of zinc and zinc-based products, and its very name was a nod to the "Horse Head" brand of high-purity zinc originally produced by the New Jersey Zinc Company, whose legacy it inherited. For much of its history, the Monaca plant was one of the largest zinc smelters in the country, a cornerstone of the local Beaver County economy that employed thousands of residents over several generations.

However, Horsehead’s most defining characteristic in its later years was its role as a major environmental services provider. It was the largest recycler of Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) dust, a hazardous waste byproduct generated by the steel industry. The company pioneered processes to heat this dust in kilns, recovering valuable zinc and other metals that could be sold and reused, thereby diverting millions of tons of hazardous material from landfills. Despite this innovative and environmentally crucial business model, the company faced significant financial headwinds, volatile commodity prices, and legacy environmental liabilities. This culminated in Horsehead Corporation filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2016, ultimately leading to the restructuring and sale of its assets, which now operate under new ownership as American Zinc Recycling. The Monaca site stands as a powerful symbol of America's industrial might, its environmental evolution, and the economic challenges of modern manufacturing.
